title: G3: innermost-bigon descent in Lemma bigon(ii) is imprecise (use innermost arc-bounded region)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap (G3): the innermost-bigon descent in Lemma `lem:bigon`(ii) conflates "innermost $\alpha\beta$-bigon" with "region with arc-only boundary".**

In the proof of Lemma `lem:bigon`(ii) (no two arcs cross more than once), the argument is:

> "Among all sub-bigons cut out by $\alpha\cup\beta$, choose one, $B$, that is innermost, i.e. whose interior contains no crossing point of $M$; such a bigon exists because any crossing inside a bigon subdivides it into smaller bigons, and we descend to a minimal one."

The descent is imprecise. A **third** arc $\eta$ passing through the bigon $B$ does *not* subdivide $B$ into smaller $\alpha\beta$-bigons: the resulting sub-regions can have boundary using three different arcs ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\eta$). So "descend to a minimal $\alpha\beta$-bigon free of crossings" is not automatic, and one must also verify (Jordan curve / proper embedding) that any strand entering $B$ must exit it.

The **conclusion** is correct, but the clean phrasing is: among all bounded complementary regions of $M$ whose entire frontier consists of arc-segments (no axis), choose one of **minimal area** (it exists since $M$ is a finite arc system, hence a finite planar graph with finitely many faces). That innermost arc-bounded region contradicts Lemma `lem:bigon`(i) (which forbids region-boundary components with crossing-point endpoints / no axis ends).

This also tightens the related step in §enum ("Inadmissibility of $N$" and the dimension cap), where the triangular region of three pairwise-interleaving arcs must be argued to be a *genuine* complementary region with arc-only boundary.
